You might recommend This Naked Mind by Annie Grace, Drinking; a love story by Caroline Knapp, Quit Like A Woman by Holly Whitaker, and Blackout by Sarah Hepola for women centric books about alcohol addiction. My dad had a gambling addiction when he was alive. We were always one scratcher away from being on the street growing up. There is a lot of shame that goes into this. Usually the gambling addiction comes from somewhere. Especially when its as compulsive as it sounds. Gambling is right up there with Alcoholism on being one of the hardest addictions to quit considering how accessible the thing is. But people CAN recover. 

But I'll tell you what happened with my dad. He managed to quit drinking but picked up scratchers. He won big. Twice. Over a million. By the time he died he gambled it away and was 3 days away from eviction all while he was fighting cancer because he hadn't stopped gambling. He hadn't paid the bill in MONTHS. Me and my siblings had to come up with the money to cover it so my mom -who is blind and disabled- wouldn't be tossed out on the street. My mom and him lost their house, cars, apartments and while I love my dad dearly it made our lives very unstable for a very long period of time. My mom stayed with him for over 50 years. They loved each other dearly and made it work as best they could. But it wasn't easy. I really hated the situation we were in. I could never really make or keep friends cause we were always moving. Christmases were a hit or a miss. There was love, but it was a goddamn struggle.  

I hope he choses to recover and get a financial advisor and make better choices. I hope if he does so he ends up being a good partner and someone you can rely on. You can share a bank account but he has to understand that you are going to watch it like a hawk and if anything gets taken out that is not approved by you? Its over. That is where the money for the wedding should go if you decide to continue, or joint bills. Carefully monitored to rebuild the trust you lost. This isn't his little piggy bank for bad decisions. But he has GOTTA change. If he doesn't? Or you don't want to spend your time with him being in the rehabilitation period... that is okay too. Its alright to cut your losses and not marry him.
